profile.name: Nae Nae
profile.tagline: A viral 2013 hip-hop dance inspired by a 1990s sitcom character.
profile.insight: Rooted in a 1990s sitcom character, the Nae Nae exploded across Vine and YouTube in 2013 before becoming a staple of viral sports celebrations.
profile.profile: The Nae Nae is a hip-hop dance move invented in 2013 by the Atlanta group We Are Toonz with their song "Drop That NaeNae". The movement is defined by placing one arm in the air and swaying from side to side. It draws direct inspiration from Sheneneh Jenkins, an exaggerated character played by Martin Lawrence on the 1990s sitcom Martin. Throughout 2014, the dance achieved massive viral popularity on social media platforms like Vine and YouTube, eventually crossing into mainstream culture via Silentó's 2015 single "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)".
profile.profile_long: The Nae Nae emerged from Atlanta hip-hop culture in 2013 when the group We Are Toonz released their hit song "Drop That NaeNae". The dance move was explicitly inspired by a character from the 1990s television sitcom Martin, specifically the sassy "ghetto girl" persona Sheneneh Jenkins portrayed by comedian Martin Lawrence in cross-dress. Group member Callamar noted in interviews that the dance encapsulated a funny club-goer persona. Throughout 2014, the dance swept across digital spaces, saturating platforms like Vine, Twitter, Instagram, and YouTube. Its physical execution involves a distinct posture: placing one arm high in the air while swaying the body from side to side. By 2015, the Nae Nae gained an even wider international footprint when American rapper Silentó featured it heavily in his debut single, "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)". Beyond viral internet videos, the Nae Nae permeated professional sports, performed as a celebratory move by athletes at collegiate and professional events. Prominent figures including NBA players, musicians, and politicians like Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama were captured performing or praising the dance. The cultural penetration of the Nae Nae was further solidified when it was integrated as a playable dance move into the video game NBA 2K16.
